page.layout: One page of running text in a single column, on the right-hand side of the scan. No marginal notes, no footnotes. Running head and page number at the top. Text runs off the right edge of the scan. No catchword or signature.

main_text.p: plectitur, quibus nimirum adductus Plan-cus obtemperare Ciceroni velit: defum-ptas ab utili, & autoritate Ciceronis.Conclusio officij promissione absoluitur. Has ergo secuti partes ad superiores literas exhortatorias respondebimus hoc modo.

p.i: I. Perquàm gratæ mihi tuæ acceptæq; extiterunt literæ.
II. Nam & animum in me benevolum prom-ptumq; declararunt: & verò adhortationem conti-nuerunt longè saluberrimam.
III. Respondissem ad eas citius, nisi te nescio quo profectum esse audivissem.
IIII. Neque enim officium in te ullum sine magna ἀχαριστίας[?] reprehensione intermittere me posse intelligo.
V. Et quidem rei huius causas habeo plurimas & maximas: vel paternæ amicitiæ: vel meæ in te observantiæ: vel deniq; beneficiorum, quæ in me hactenus contulisti, & adhuc confers quotidie.
VI. Itaq; etiam atq; etiam rogo, hoc tibi persuadeas, unum te esse, quem parentis ego loco colam: & in quo spem meam omnem fixam locatamq; habeam.
VII. Operam me quoq; daturum: ut tua apud me monita, & prudentiæ, & fidelitatis plena, eum quem debent locum inveniant: nec in capessenda Rep. officio defuisse meo cuiq; videar.

page.notes: The text is cut off at the right edge of the scan, so the line ends of the last paragraph are not visible beyond "Per-". The Greek word in IIII. is hard to read: the printed form looks like ἀχαεισίας or ἀχαρισίας; I have transcribed it as ἀχαριστίας with a doubt mark. The ff in "Refpondiffem", "nifi" and "audiuiffem" is a double long s, rendered as ss. The line "Conclusio" is printed as "Con" at the line end and "clusio" on the next line, with no hyphen, so it is written whole. The space after "Ciceronis." is missing in the print, and I have kept it that way.
